CUDA terminal-fence candidate: complete fixed-matrix decision
=============================================================

The complete candidate is inconclusive under the unchanged 5% policy. Retain the production CUDA baseline and the expanded completion test coverage; do not adopt a selected size, backend or mode, retry the trial, or correct by framework controls.

Measured baseline source: ``84c88c98c895103395e1b6d6e98f7618848a14d3`` (tree ``57a755d537e516b91c70c1b555f2803753389862``).
Measured candidate source: ``32fd10a941e783c703d6cc971bf7f18b0cc71c7a`` (tree ``e97ff69a80c3ab8ae1d74fc9da8e76940ee7fea2``).

The candidate removes one final stream fence after the source-matched final scalar/status readback. Resource ownership, exception completion guard, DeviceGuard, arithmetic, workspace sizes and explicit backend/mode selection remain unchanged. Source identities describe the measured candidates even if production later retains the baseline.

Protocol and interpretation
---------------------------

All 32 original CUDA configurations and all 336 primary case/implementation rows are retained, including 128 PyTorch CUDA controls, 128 cuda-native rows and 80 cuda-cublas rows. Two windows execute ABBA and BAAB in fresh worker processes; window two reverses configuration order. There are 512 raw artifacts and 5,376 stored candidate-case outcomes. Every side has eight process blocks, each with three warmups, 36 Williams-balanced rounds and one repetition. Each row therefore contributes 288 measured rounds per side. The boundary pause is 60 seconds; telemetry is captured only before/after each child.

The primary estimate is the median of all normalized rounds pooled across the eight blocks on each side, then current/baseline. It is not the median of eight process medians. The original comparator resamples artifact blocks and then rounds (10,000 resamples, seed 20261018, 95% percentile interval). Upper bound <= 1.05 supports no material regression; lower bound > 1.05 is a regression; all overlap is inconclusive. Every primary row, including controls, participates in the overall decision. No filtering, retry, pooling of earlier trials, control correction, work normalization or partial mode/size adoption is applied.

Fresh API constructs resources per call. Session reuses explicitly owned CUDA resources. Prepared reuses prepared solve state. Their measurements and verdicts are reported separately; scope medians are never subtracted to infer component costs.

Numerical and completion evidence
---------------------------------

A separate, complete 64-process CUDA preflight finished before timing: 672 candidate-case rows, two independent residual checks per row (1,344 checks), and exact same-candidate iterations/matvecs/restarts and thresholds across both sources and repeated reuse. Timing artifacts retain candidate/case correctness summaries from the collector's checks outside timing before/after collection. Every retained summary passes its independent true-residual gate and matches the preflight fixture/work identity; individual timed sample invocations are not separately residual-instrumented. Convergence and work are audited separately; no iteration normalization is used.

Both actual C++ CUDA test binaries passed memcheck with full leak checking and synccheck: each run executed 37 tests, with 36 passing and the one expected multi-GPU skip on this host. The candidate completion test queries a borrowed nondefault nonblocking stream immediately after solve, before helper synchronization, download, reset or destruction. Its 184 solves span terminal iteration limits 0/1, initially converged, negative curvature, nonfinite inputs, restart paths, host/device execution, native/cuBLAS, fusion and supported algorithm/preconditioner combinations. Exception synchronization and borrowed resource lifetime remain covered.

Sixteen fixed same-call captures pair ten observed calls after three warmups for cuBLAS Jacobi n=1024 fresh API/Session/prepared in host/device mode, plus native Jacobi fresh API host/device. All 80 paired calls show exactly one fewer cudaStreamSynchronize, cudaGetDevice and cudaSetDevice; launch/memcpy/memset API counts and physical GPU kernel/copy inventories match. The final source-matched copy has two subsequent synchronizations in A and one in B. The analysis retains exact API table/name/thread records, inclusive/deepest phase ownership, unassigned events and physical event context. The D2H designation is source-matched ordering inference rather than decoded API arguments; timestamp containment attributes physical GPU events. Instrumented timings are not framework scores.

CPU candidate disposition
-------------------------

The independent CPU eight-accumulator candidate abd655a was rejected before timing. Dense-64 native changed stable I/M/R from 49/51/0 to 48/50/0 in both untimed repeats; all independent true-residual gates passed. This is a fixed-work contract rejection, not measured evidence of a slowdown. All three CPU timing plans remain pristine and cancelled. No CPU size/mode fallback, timing retry or work correction was used; production retains the CPU baseline.

---------------------------------------------

The following counts use native/PyTorch pooled medians from the same artifacts. A ratio above one means a higher native median. They are descriptive, with no new interval or adoption score, and do not adjust the primary A/B comparison. Limits
------

These intervals describe this measured host and these supplied blocks. Eight processes are not eight independent physical-host replications. A 60-second boundary pause and boundary telemetry do not establish thermal stability or absence of WSL/background contention. Within-block serial dependence can make round bootstrap intervals too narrow; per-row 95% intervals do not establish simultaneous family-wise coverage. Earlier A/A and A/B outcomes remain disclosed and unpooled. Controls reveal context but cannot rescue a failed native row, and a changing control does not by itself identify the cause of a native change. No unsupported kernel-only, allocation-only, scope-difference or universal NumPy/PyTorch speedup claim follows from this campaign.
